written.myAnswer: A small fire should be tackled with a suitable portable fire extinguisher by someone trained to use it, without panic or putting anyone in danger.
Emergency drills prepare students to respond appropriately and without panic when an emergency occurs.

Raise the alarm and inform the teacher or laboratory in-charge. If it is safe, switch off the electricity supply. Do not use water; use a suitable extinguisher, such as CO₂, only if trained and safe to do so. Evacuate if the fire cannot be controlled safely.
Keep a suitable fire extinguisher available and ensure students know where it is and how to use it. Ensure everyone knows the location and operation of the safety shower.

Immediately alert the teacher or laboratory in-charge, keep others away, and avoid touching or attempting to clean up the spill. If the chemical has spilled onto the student, use the safety shower to flush the affected area thoroughly and remove contaminated clothing while seeking help. Keep ignition sources away and evacuate if the area is unsafe.
